The metrics useful for quantifying the value for a distribution system employing the SSTs will be developed by NREL team. The NREL team will refine the use case scenarios and performance metrics with Eaton team and the utility, as available, to ensure that they capture boundary conditions of operations. Estimated completion: 6 months from project start. The focus of the work is to analyze the value of MV SST on the distribution feeder in the presence of high EV penetration. Furthermore, the study also considers the addition of PV and energy storage to support high EV charging on the grid. Sites for large EV charging capacity are considered in this study. The EV and PV penetration considered in the work are defined here. EV penetration: The percentage of maximum coincident EV charging power over peak feeder load. Comparative study of the two scenarios is performed to explore the benefits of SST on the grid. Use case scenario 1: Scenario with EV Several EV charging sites are selected at certain distances across the feeder to enable high power EV charging stations. In this scenario, the EV charging loads are added at specific sites on the feeder. Time-series power flow simulation is conducted for a day simulating the maximum coincident EV charging to investigate the impact of high EV charging demand on the feeder. Different power system parameters are measured, and the performance of the grid operation is evaluated through a set of metrics. Use case scenario 2: Scenario with EV and MV SST In this scenario, the conventional transformers at the EV charging sites are replaced by MV SSTs. Time-series power flow study with the same EV charging demand as scenario 1 is conducted, and the performance metrics are evaluated. 7 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Use Case Analysis with J1 Feeder: The use cases implementation on the J1 feeder starts with the selection of suitable EV charging sites. Fig. 4 presents the selected five EV charging sites (A, B, C, D, and E) on the J1 feeder. The 3 phase nodes, voltage level, and the distance between the sites are considered in the site selection. The sites consist of 150 kW level EV chargers; Sites A and B include 12 charging ports each while sites C, D, and E have 10 ports each. Figure 5 shows the aggregated EV charging profiles at each site, and Fig. 6 represents the total aggregated EV charging on the feeder. EV penetration is 50% in this case.
